hero.title: Customers, hours and invoices. On your terms.
hero.subtitle: Haij is an open source business platform for solo consultants and micro-businesses. Danish-first, hosted in the EU, and built so you can take all of your data with you the day you want to.
hero.trust: Open source · AGPL-3.0 · Data in the EU

values.danishBody: CVR lookups, Danish invoicing rules and VAT are the starting point, not an adaptation. The platform speaks Danish because your business does.
values.dataBody: Everything runs on EU-owned infrastructure, and you can export your entire organization at any time. No lock-in, no fine print.
values.securityBody: Passkeys and two-factor authentication from day one, tenant isolation enforced in the database itself, and every change in an audit trail.

landing.status: In open development. The foundation is in place; CRM and time tracking are the next modules.

about.title: About Haij
about.subtitle: Which build of the platform is running here, and whether the database has kept up.
about.dirtyHint: Built from a working tree with uncommitted changes, so the commit does not tell the whole truth about the code that is running.
about.releaseHint: The version number is raised by hand when a step is worth naming. The commit is stamped in at build time and points at exactly the code answering here.
about.schemaHint: The number of migrations the build was made from, against the number the database has applied.
about.schemaBehindHint: The database has fewer migrations than the code expects. Run the migrations before using the system further.
about.license: Haij is open source under AGPL-3.0.

numbering.title: Invoice numbering
numbering.hint: The next invoice gets this number. Set it to your previous system's next number when you move in. It can only be raised, never lowered.
numbering.label: Next invoice number
numbering.savedToast: The next invoice will be number {number}.
numbering.tooLow: The number must be higher than the current one. The sequence has to stay unbroken.

roleRates.companyHint: Rates in DKK excl. VAT. A rate here applies to every hour on this customer unless the project has its own.
roleRates.projectHint: Rates in DKK excl. VAT. These override what the customer is otherwise agreed at.
roleRates.empty: No agreed rates. Hours are priced at the customer's ordinary rate.
roleRates.emptyNoRoles: Create a role under company settings first.
roleRates.invalid: Pick a role and enter a rate, e.g. 1,400.

list.noUnbilledTime: There are no unbilled hours to invoice.

editor.title: Invoice draft
editor.issueBody: The invoice gets the next sequential number and is locked. Only the status can change afterwards, and corrections require a credit note.
editor.issueNoLines: Add at least one line before issuing.
editor.issueNoProfile: Fill in your company profile under Settings before issuing.
editor.profileMissingBody: Invoices must carry your company name, CVR and address.
editor.deleteBody: The draft and its lines are removed. Any time entries pulled in become unbilled again.
editor.noLines: No lines yet. Add the first one.
editor.lineInvalid: Check quantity and price. Use e.g. 1.5 and 950.00.
editor.regroupNoTime: There are no time entries on this draft to group.
editor.previewHint: This is how the invoice looks. The parties and dates are the ones stamped on at issue; the number is assigned then too.

ai.title: AI
ai.subtitle: The language model behind upcoming AI features, e.g. signal scoring.
ai.providerHint: Chosen in .env on the server. Keys never live in the database or the code.
ai.setupIntro: AI is not set up yet. Add a few lines to your .env and restart the app:
ai.setupOutro: Mistral is EU-hosted (Paris). Ollama runs locally, so data never leaves the machine.
ai.failAuth: The key was rejected. Check MISTRAL_API_KEY in your .env and restart the app.
ai.failUnreachable: The service did not answer. Check network and address.
ai.failGeneric: Something went wrong. Try again and check the server log if it persists.
ai.principleSovereign: EU-hosted or local models only. The provider can be swapped without touching the rest of the platform.
ai.principleApproval: AI never sends anything out of the house. Everything it drafts requires your approval first.
ai.principleUsage: The first use is the phase 4 signals engine, scoring opportunities against your service profile.

signals.title: Signals
signals.emptyHint: Hit Refresh to pull new signals from your sources.
signals.unconfiguredTitle: The signals engine is not set up yet

signals.convertedToast: The signal is linked to a customer.

add.title: Save as signal
add.hint: For anything you spot yourself, e.g. a LinkedIn post or a conversation. Paste a link and notes; the signal is scored and followed up like the automatic ones.
add.invalid: Check the fields. CVR must be 8 digits, the link must be a valid URL.

settings.title: Signals
settings.hint: The signals engine looks for organizations resembling your customers and scores what it finds against your service profile.
settings.profileHint: The text the AI measures everything against. Write what you sell, to whom, and what makes a good and a bad signal. The more concrete, the less noise.
settings.profilePlaceholder:
We help larger Danish organizations with…

Typical customers are…

A good signal is…

A bad signal is…
settings.feedsHint: RSS and Atom feeds to follow. Job postings count: most job sites expose a saved search as a feed. Test each source as you add it.
settings.feedsMax: There is room for ten sources. Remove one to add another.
settings.checkEmpty: The feed parses but holds no articles right now.
settings.checkNotFeed: That address answers with an ordinary web page, not a feed. Look for an RSS icon, or try /rss or /feed on the end.
settings.checkUnreachable: Could not reach that address. Check the spelling.
settings.sourcesHint: Beyond your own sources the engine searches CVR and the EU tender database.
settings.cvrHelp: The first four digits of the DB07 code. New companies in these branches become signals.
settings.tedHelp: Tenders mentioning one of these words are pulled in.
settings.rssLabel: RSS feeds (one per line, optionally "url | name")
